newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Namoi Cotton reports rising profits.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Namoi Cotton reports rising profits.

text.p: Leading Australian cotton processor and marketer Namoi Cotton Co-operative said on Friday it achieved an after-tax profit of slightly more than A$6.0 million for the year ended February 1997 and is projecting strongly improving results to 1999.
In 1996 Namoi Cotton, a grower-owned organisation, recorded a profit of just over A$1.0 million following a period of almost four years of drought-affected seasons.
The 1997 Australian cotton crop, currently being harvested, was projected to reach a record 2.5 million 500 pound bales, almost a third bigger than last year's crop, Namoi said in a statement.
A promising water situation suggested a similar size crop may be on the cards in 1998 which would be a further boon for Namoi and the Australian cotton industry, it said.
Namoi Cotton chairman Stuart Boydell said the result was well-earned and provided for more strengthening of the balance sheet of the co-operative.
Chief executive officer Allan Jones said prospects for the 1997 crop, which would be reflected in 1997/98 results, were very bright.
Namoi Cotton, which is based in the northern section of New South Wales state, would return to its position as the largest cotton processor this season, he said.

Namoi ginned just 458,000 bales last year, well below its one million bales capacity because of drought. It operated just six of its 12 gins in 1995, eight in 1996 and has 11 facilities operating this year.
Operating at well under half capacity last year, Namoi accounted for almost 25 percent of ginning of the total Australian crop of 1.89 million bales and 60 percent of proiduction in its areas.
